# NOTES: TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1: The Case of the Black Twenty-Two (Brian Flynn, 1929; Grosset & Dunlap)

**Chars:** Peter Daventry (junior partner, Merryweather, Linnell & Daventry, Solicitors, Cornhill; Oxford man; hungover). David Linnell (senior partner, 58, Lancashire). Plunkett (clerk, 35 yrs). Merryweather (founder, dead 7 yrs). Laurence P. Stewart (US millionaire, Chicago/Wall St, widower, collector of Royal relics, believes descended from Mary Queen of Scots; Assynton Lodge, Assynton, Berkshire, near Wantage). Charles Stewart (son, ~22). Marriott (Peter's friend). Gustave (Violette waiter). Lironi (Violette proprietor). Forshaw (Ronald, young Day, Forshaw & Palmers). Mr. Day (tall partner). Detective-Inspector Goodall (stout, clean-shaven, blue serge). Druce (wizened night-watchman, 60, 6 yrs service; daughter Poppy). James "Jim" Mason (night-watchman, murdered). Mrs. Turner (cleaner). Doctor Archer. Sergeant Amos Clegg (Assynton; wife 17 yrs married). Doctor Gunner. Morgan Llewellyn (secretary, early 30s, pince-nez, reddish-brown eyes, Welsh). John Butterworth (butler, 60+, ex-Sir Julian Kennedy, Washington; wife housekeeper, married 37 yrs). Marjorie Lennox (ward, petite, retroussé nose, blue eyes). Maids Barton, Regan, Evans, Winter; cook Mrs. Briggs; gardener Maidment; boot-boy Patrick O'Connor (18, b. 17 March); father Michael O'Connor (foundry, black beard, 6ft2). P.C. Potter. Colonel Leach-Fletcher (60s, white moustache, Bentley, house "Neuve Chapelle", Rockinge road). Anthony Bathurst (free-lance, Uppingham/Oxford, squash at Princes, grey eyes). Gerald Daventry (Peter's brother, accountant, Wedderburn & Rathbone). Rosemary Armitage (Charles's love, The Towers, 7 miles). Blanchard (Blanchard's Hotel, Clifford St; fair, stout, protruding eyes). Atkins (porter). Rabjohns (chambermaid). Waring (Goodall's assistant). "Snoop" Mortimer / "Flash Alf" (NY crook, alias Laurence Charles Stewart). Alice Mortimer (née Butterworth, hay fever, black glasses). Andrew Ferguson (Crake & Ferguson, NY; arrives via Mauretania). Emily (maid at Bathurst's flat).

**Events in order:**
1. Ch I: Peter hungover in Cornhill. Linnell: Stewart's letter (dated June 7, 192–) asks firm to buy at Day, Forshaw & Palmers' sale (June 10, Hanover Galleries, W.1; Lord Clavering's collection, Clavering Court, Warwickshire): No.37 "Collar of Pearls", No.38 "Antique Tapestry Fire-screen", No.39 "Rosary of Amber Beads", "all having been indisputably the property of Mary, Queen of Scots." No price limit. At Violette lunch, Peter meets Marriott; man & woman at next table. Peter says "So's Mary, Queen of Scots" (replying to Marriott's "Queen Anne's dead"); man knocks cruet to floor; woman's warning look. Overheard: woman "Take my advice—let's go to-morrow—not to-day." Man: "Can't see it makes much difference."
2. Ch II: Peter views items; two plain-clothes men watch. Screen ~3.5–4 ft on carved pedestal; beads spell "JESUS CHRIST, GOD AND SAVIOUR"; corners: Scots Lion (top-left), fleur-de-lis (top-right), Leopards & Lilies (bottom). Peter tips attendant. Linnell suspects forgery. Telegrams from Stewart: "Say what the hell's biting you—when I say Buy—then Buy. Got that? Stewart." and "Say—you don't look before you leap—you take a magnifying glass. Same name as before." Peter dines at Club (Isthmian; show "On Approval") that evening.
3. Ch III: Linnell at Galleries next morning: Mason murdered, three items stolen. Goodall interviews. Watchmen: Mason on from midnight; Druce relieved ~11:55. Woman had asked Druce/Mason opening time (10 o'clock) and way to Marble Arch; sneezed walking away. Office door unlocked. Four keys (Day, each partner, Forshaw). Linnell gets phone call from Peter: Stewart found dead in Assynton library, skull battered.
4. Ch IV: Charles phoned Cornhill. Secretary's name Morgan/Llewellyn. Charles asked to cancel purchases; later asked for private detective ("efficient, discreet, trustworthy"). Peter proposes Anthony Bathurst (Gerald's Oxford friend; Considine Manor case in Sussex). Peter finds Bathurst at Princes; Bathurst: meet at Paddington 6:55; "bring a revolver."
5. Ch V: Assynton. Stewart's body in chair at desk, dressing gown over pajamas, slippers, pen nearly dropped; note "Urgent in the morning! M. L." Revolver in LEFT dressing-gown pocket, five loaded, sixth discharged. Library door locked, key inside; French doors bolted top & bottom. Stewart 53 (birthday July 22). Charles: returned ~9:45, looked in on father with Colonel Leach-Fletcher, said "Good-night." Llewellyn: last saw Stewart at dinner; spent 8:30–10 with Miss Lennox in music-room; then to bed by 10:30. Clegg finds lace handkerchief with "M. L." in curtains at French doors. Stewart's solicitors Crake & Ferguson, New York.
6. Ch VI: Marjorie Lennox (ward since age 3; father old friend of Laurence) says she left music-room ~9, went to her room, never entered library. Clegg suspects lie. Marjorie accuses Llewellyn: "The man is Morgan Llewellyn!!!" She storms out.
7. Ch VII: Butterworth: last saw Stewart at 10; Colonel left just after 10; Butterworth locked up 10:30; bolted French doors; swears key was inside. Hears Stewart's voice ~10:10 and Miss Lennox's voice in library (reveals to Goodall later). Clegg notes staff.
8. Ch VIII: Paddington. Goodall on same train (Assynton inquiry from local police). Bathurst, Peter, Goodall travel together. Bathurst: "Flattery is merely a counterfeit business." Peter recounts Violette incident. Goodall: Lironi knows the Violette. Bathurst: woman's jewel-case reflex (Holmes).
9. Ch IX: Assynton dinner (Miss Lennox absent, headache). Museum Room key normally hung in Butterworth's service room. Charles: Llewellyn's catalogue exists. ~1:22 a.m. Bathurst hears step pass; Llewellyn re-enters room next-but-one.
10. Ch X: Bathurst walks to village, meets Michael O'Connor at foundry. Patrick's bicycle (kept in Maidment's potting-shed) carries tar from road being resurfaced into Assynton; used on night of murder. Bathurst talks to Patrick in shed.
11. Ch XI: Library reconstruction with Goodall, Clegg. Goodall: "Theories are all very well." Bathurst theory: bicycle carried murderer; telephone message to hotel ~11:20; murder ~11. Coal-scuttle: seven or eight dried mud pellets and four brown stones. Ink-bowl disturbed. Bathurst's "geometry": centre Hanover Galleries, radius one mile, hotel within circle. Clegg gives Goodall the handkerchief.
12. Ch XII: Museum Room (2044 items); Crown of Charles I; Black Prince's gorget; Item 866: "Antique fire-screen, of beaten metal-work… Originally the property of Mary, Queen of Scots" missing. Marjorie describes it (Lion, fleur-de-lis, Leopards & Lilies, "Timeo Danaos" in center, big fish below, repoussé). Peter completes description. Clegg: trunk call at 11 minutes to Blanchard's Hotel, Clifford St., W.; couple checked out as Mr & Mrs Laurence Charles Stewart from New York.
13. Ch XIII: Goodall to Blanchard's; Bathurst & Peter & Goodall to Colonel Leach-Fletcher. Colonel: Stewart confided "treacherous" tampering with papers; disappointed with Charles's conduct; planned interview with son after Colonel left. Colonel drove home ~10:15 by Bentley.
14. Ch XIV: Colonel recalls Renan's "Vie de Jésus" open on Stewart's desk. Bathurst; Peter finds letter from Llewellyn to Marjorie inside book.
15. Ch XV: Letter: "Dear Incomparable Marjorie… Marry me!… Let me know your answer after dinner to-night… Morgan Llewellyn." Bathurst: Marjorie showed letter to guardian ~10:05. Peter wades pool; finds jagged path-stone (~14 in, shaped like magnum bottle) = murder weapon. Second stone in ink-bowl.
16. Ch XVI: Peter fires revolver twice (Bathurst upstairs hears nothing). Bullet found embedded in "The Memoirs of Réné de St. Maure—one-time Page to Mary Stuart" (848 pages).
17. Ch XVII: Memoir passage: "Black Twenty-Two"; Cardinal's great gift; Thibaut Girardier, Chief Armorer, made two screens (tapestry and beaten metal); Mary's "Queen-Mistress"; riddle. Bathurst leaves for London.
18. Ch XVIII: Blanchard's Hotel. Register: Stewart arrived 28 May from NY; bill ~£14; left Wed night after phone call (near relative ill). Atkins: Mrs. Stewart wore black glasses, said "my father", read clock at distance. Room 54: smell like burning; Asthma-type remnants. Bathurst hints hay fever.
19. Ch XIX: Ricardo's (Soho) supper. Bathurst shows Goodall letter, stone, bullet; promises arrest within ~48 hrs. Gives card with address.
20. Ch XX: Bathurst's research; Daily Telegraph Personal, May 30: "M. S. Ring Regent 9999 till further notice. Both well!" = Bothwell; Regent 9999 = Blanchard's. Virgil "Timeo Danaos et dona ferentes." Emily (maid) reports Peter's phone call.
21. Ch XXI: Andrew Ferguson of Crake & Ferguson arrives. Will: Marjorie £250,000 in trust till 40; Charles residue till 45; both to marry each other; third-party marriage forfeits to charity. Llewellyn £300 annuity; Butterworth £500 p.a. Goodall: NY police identify "Snoop" Mortimer / "Flash Alf."
22. Ch XXII: Inquest adjourned. Bathurst to Charles: Rosemary Armitage; father's threats; father sent Marjorie to fetch Charles ~10:15. Bathurst orders house closed; Butterworth to stay; others dismissed.
23. Ch XXIII: Car (Bentley) to Neuve Chapelle; walk to Assynton; O'Connor helps; Mortimers in library (Alice & "Snoop" searching screens). Goodall arrests "Snoop" Mortimer & Alice Mortimer for Mason's murder (June 9); arrests John Butterworth for Stewart's murder (June 8).
24. Ch XXIV: Metal screen has secret cavity behind fish; O'Connor says metal can't be punched through; Bathurst presses fish's eye and tail → cavity.
25. Ch XXV: Twenty-two black pearls of Lorraine. Bathurst's explanation: "M.L." = Merryweather, Linnell & Daventry (his mistaken reading abandoned); "ICHTHUS" from Greek of "Jesus Christ God Saviour" (I, CH, TH, S = Ichthus = Fish). Alice née Butterworth. Charles to marry Rosemary; Marjorie gets pearls as wedding gift. "The End."

Transcriber notes at end: spelling fixes listed (not content).

## BOOK 2: Thomas Wingfold, Curate, Vol. I (George MacDonald; "END OF THE FIRST VOLUME")

**Chars:** Helen Lingard (23, tall, blue eyes, dark hair, fair skin, over-still face; orphan of Indian army officer father; mother died at her birth; raised by aunt; brother Leopold ("Poldie") 3 yrs younger, Cambridge, Hindoo-mother's eyes). Mrs. Ramshorn (aunt, widow of Dean of Halystone; peevish mouth; holds Helen's fortune). George Bascombe (cousin; son of canon of northern cathedral; barrister-in-training; tall, handsome, self-proclaimed prophet against beliefs; sings own song "Each man has his lampful"). Thomas Wingfold (26, curate of Glaston abbey church; rector non-resident; uncle Dr. Jonah Driftwood D.D. left 157 sermons; brother dead; reads Horace; shy). Joseph Polwarth (gate-keeper at Osterfield Park "Park-Gate"; deformed, large chest, asthma; Cornish ancestry; brother Robert dead; wrote anonymous letter about Jeremy Taylor). Rachel Polwarth (niece; 4 ft; crooked; hair rich brown; sings; ~£20/yr). Mr. Faber (doctor). Mr. Bird (old doctor, dead). Emmeline (victim, Yorkshire, manufacturer's family, flaxen; engaged to Captain Hodges). Jones (groom). Fanny (Helen's horse); the "old horse". Mr. Drew (linendraper). Lord de Barre (owner; "new earl" building house).

**Events in order:**
1. Ch I: November, wind; Helen bored, sleeps.
2. Ch II: Wingfold walks by river Lythe; sits on stone; reads Horace.
3. Ch III: Dinner at Mrs. Ramshorn's (Friday). Bascombe arrives; curate invited. Helen's looks described.
4. Ch IV: Talk: poetry; Bascombe's song; Helen dislikes heathenish sound; "Don't you think?" habit of Wingfold.
5. Ch V: Moonlit walk; Bascombe: "Do you believe one word of all that?"; "Your silence is honesty."
6. Ch VI: Wingfold on gravestone in churchyard; doubts; determines to study.
7. Ch VII: Bascombe's character (prophet of new order); Helen's education.
8. Ch VIII: Garden talk; Bascombe on death, duty, punishment, "mutual compassion."
9. Ch IX: Park; old Glaston house by lake; secret trap-room in closet (Helen & Leopold's childhood haunt; legend of lady drowned in sack).
10. Ch X: Meet Polwarths (dwarf niece & uncle); Bascombe: they should not marry; Sunday church; sermon on forgiveness; Mrs. Ramshorn: "some injuries… no, that I never would [forget]."
11. Ch XI: Wingfold's agony; prayer fails; reads uncle's sermons.
12. Ch XII: Returns Rachel's dropped manuscript; "Do not be alarmed: I have not read one word of it."
13. Ch XIII: Bascombe courts Helen; she "liked" him.
14. Ch XIV: Letter from "Joseph Polwarth, The Park-Gate": uncle's sermon was Jeremy Taylor's; Wingfold admits he never knew.
15. Ch XV: Visits Park Gate; Rachel answers door; tea.
16. Ch XVI: Polwarth's attic study.
17. Ch XVII: Polwarth's plan: Wingfold should confess and use others' sermons honestly; Polwarth: "Was Jesus true?" Rachel stays.
18. Ch XVIII: Polwarth's life: schooling, deformity, boy in pond, secret den, Matthew 1:21 ("Thou shalt call his name Jesus…") turns him to Christ.
19. Ch XIX: Polwarth: go to the New Testament "to find out"; Wingfold keeps curacy a month.
20. Ch XX: Wingfold's "confessing" sermon; Mrs. Ramshorn disapproves; Bascombe approves.
21. Ch XXI: Leopold taps Helen's window ~midnight; face of ghost; blood on wristband; "Helen, I am a murderer."
22. Ch XXII: Leopold: "They are after me." Helen hides him; takes knife (skean-dhu, name engraved on silver); bread and wine.
23. Ch XXIII: Helen takes him to hidden room in deserted house. Whistle signal. Leopold has drug (silver box).
24. Ch XXIV: Dawn; Helen hides secret at breakfast; birthday of aunt; cap; no friend to consult.
25. Ch XXV: Helen daylight visit; sees Rachel singing; prays "I am his sister, thou knowest."
26. Ch XXVI: Leopold's story: Emmeline's manipulation; drug use at Cambridge.
27. Ch XXVII: Ball, cloak, black silk mask; note "Meet me for one long minute at the circle"; Emmeline: "I am going to be married to Captain Hodges"; Leopold stabs her with knife; flees; Helen is his refuge. Newspaper: "mysterious murder of a young lady in Yorkshire."
28. Ch XXVIII: Helen: "I would rather be you than she." Takes knife. Resolves to protect him.
29. Ch XXIX: Leopold brain-fever; Helen moves him to her room; Mrs. Ramshorn helps; Dr. Faber (cold, unbelieving) attends; weeks of nursing.
30. Ch XXX: Wingfold studies NT with Polwarth; Polwarth: Jesus came primarily to... ; miracles ("the question is not Are the miracles true? but Was Jesus true?").
31. Ch XXXI: Wingfold: "Why call ye me Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?" John 7:17. Sermon confessing he never did one thing Jesus told him. Helen sees him; Mrs. Ramshorn calls him Socinian; Bascombe impressed. Polwarth weeps joyfully.
32. Ch XXXII: Leopold asks for Bascombe; Helen shrinks from bringing Bascombe in; she now hopes Leopold innocent (dream/drug hallucination).
33. Ch XXXIII: Helen and Bascombe ride in park at sunset; Bascombe's views on death and immortality; he discusses the girl-in-ball-dress murder on the Yorkshire coast; coast-guard saw boat; murderer possibly fled to Holland; Bascombe: "I should like to try the unravelling of it." Helen turns home. "END OF THE FIRST VOLUME."
